items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Fernand never had a band of regular musicians although there were certain ones that usually gigged with him and I did a few with him.

ctx.x: The Renaissance Ballroom at the corner of 138th Street and 7th Avenue was a place where most of the Negro clubs held their dances and the leader of the orchestra was a fellow named Fernand Andrade, a banjo and guitar player. Fernand never had a band of regular musicians although there were certain ones that usually gigged with him and I did a

few with him. There are many name musicians in the 20s and 30s that gigged at one time with Fernand; Benny Carter, Rex Stewart, Bobby Starke, etc. When I gigged with Fernand, I met one of the greatest alto sax men in the business. His name was Hilton Jefferson. Jeff was a very quiet man but he made his horn talk for him and all the musicians loved him.

Another musician that always had the highest paid gigs was a drummer named Peek-a-Boo Jimmy. Peek-a-Boo had played with James P. Johnson, Willie 'The Lion' Smith and 'Lucky' Roberts in the days before I even dreamed of going to New York. I gigged with Peek-a-Boo twice and both times it was really enjoyable. The music we played was not very jazzy because Jimmy was a drummer who had lost sight of what the other drummers were doing. And most of the musicians he hired were a certain age and not up to date on jazz…
